synopsis: Lor’themar and Liadrin travel with Rommath, Lethira, and a Blood Knight honor guard, including Falanaras, by magical transport into Horde-held Lordaeron before completing the approach to Undercity on foot through the ruined courtyard, old throne room, and elevators into the Forsaken capital. Forsaken escorts including Serenya frame the road with old ranger wounds. Their audience with Sylvanas formalizes the understanding reached at Windrunner Spire in the Banshee Queen’s seat of power, where Varimathras’s demonic presence stands in sharp relief and Sylvanas presents herself as both undead ruler and former Ranger-General with an active interest in Quel’Thalas’s defense. After Lethira and Falanaras privately reckon with how differently Sylvanas inhabits her ancestral ruin and her undead capital, Thrall, Cairne, Vol’jin, and the other Horde leaders gather in council to weigh Silvermoon’s admission. Old grievances, orcish fear of fel corruption, Vol’jin’s distinction between Darkspear caution and Amani hatred, Sylvanas’s advocacy, and unease over M’uru and the Blood Knights all collide. The Horde calls for a controlled duel in the ruined courtyard above Undercity to judge the order through one representative. Falanaras faces Gorath Stonebinder, an orc shaman whose spiritual authority and suspicion of corrupt power make him a demanding examiner. Gorath presses him with earth, wind, and lightning, testing whether Falanaras can carry formidable Blood Knight power through resistance while remaining tactically precise, obedient to the duel’s terms, and honorable in victory. Falanaras combines spellbreaker instincts, two-handed swordcraft, barriers, and overwhelming red-gold force to defeat Gorath, then holds a lethal stroke because the agreed contest forbids killing and ends at yield. The display proves the Blood Knights’ military value and disciplined control without dispelling the moral suspicion surrounding their power. The Horde formally admits the blood elves despite sharp reservations, with Thrall invoking the Forsaken as another controversial ally judged by proof and necessity. Admission gives Silvermoon legal membership before trust or belonging can follow.
title: Chapter 17: Admission to the Horde
